match.reason: None of the bank points teaches solving inequalities or the sign-flip rule for multiplying or dividing by a negative; they all cover equations, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Solving linear inequalities
card: An inequality compares two sides with <, >, ≤ or ≥. Its solution is a range of values, not one number.
Solve it like an equation. Do the same thing to both sides: add, subtract, multiply or divide.
If you multiply or divide both sides by a negative number, flip the sign. < becomes > and ≤ becomes ≥. Adding or subtracting never flips it.
Example: −2x < 6. Divide both sides by −2 and flip the sign, so x > −3. Check with x = 0: −2 × 0 = 0, and 0 < 6 is true.
draft.remember: Solve as you would an equation, but flip the sign when you multiply or divide by a negative.

a.why: Divide both sides by −3 and flip the sign, so x ≤ −4. The option x ≥ −4 divides correctly but forgets to flip the sign. Check x = −5: −3 × −5 = 15, and 15 ≥ 12 is true.
a.clue: Which way does the sign go after dividing by a negative?

b.why: Subtract 5 from both sides: −2x > 6. Divide by −2 and flip the sign: x < −3. The option x > −3 forgets the flip. Check x = −4: 5 − 2 × −4 = 13, and 13 > 11 is true.
b.clue: Subtracting 5 does not flip the sign. Dividing by −2 does.

check.summary: No problems found. Both questions have one correct answer (x ≤ −4 and x < −3), and the card, clues and explanations are accurate and stay within this point.
